To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum theoretical yield for 1, 3-PD production from glycerol is 0.75 mol/mol, that this yield can be improved to 0.86 mol/mol by cofermentation of glucose or xylose, and that the yield is limited by the rate of glycerol uptake and the rate of NADH oxidation by glycerol dehydrogenase.

1,3-propanediol (an important intermediate in chemical and plastic synthesis) can be produced in high yields from glycerol, and that this yield can be increased by cofermentation with glucose or xylose.
we have engineered a microbe to coferment glucose and/or xylose with glycerol to increase the yield of 1.3-propanediol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a microbial system for the production of 1, 3-propanediol from glycerol and other carbon sources.
the development of an improved process for the production of 1, 3-propanediol.
the engineering of a biochemical pathway to enhance 1,3-propanediol production from renewable resources.
